item.title: [planForChange] SharePoint: HTML pages
item.description:
[What and Why:]

SharePoint is adding support for HTML pages. Users will be able to create HTML pages with Copilot in SharePoint or upload HTML from another source. After an HTML page is stored in the Site Pages library, users can render it as a page in SharePoint, make additional edits, publish it, and share it with their audience.

This gives organizations another way to present content alongside existing ASPX pages and helps users create polished web content more efficiently in SharePoint.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Public Preview: Rollout will begin in early October 2026 and is expected to complete in early October 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • SharePoint authors who create, upload, edit, publish, or share pages.
  • Users with access to Copilot in SharePoint for HTML page creation and editing.
  • Admins and support teams responsible for SharePoint authoring guidance and Copilot adoption.

Platforms/Services:

  • SharePoint Online
  • Copilot in SharePoint
  • Site Pages library

What will happen:

  • Users can create HTML pages in SharePoint by selecting + New on a SharePoint site and then selecting HTML page.
  • Users can create an HTML page with Copilot from the floating Copilot button on a SharePoint site.
  • Users can create an HTML page from the Publish landing page by selecting + Create and then HTML page.
  • Users can describe the page they want in the prompt box and attach relevant files for additional context.
  • Copilot can create a draft HTML page and open it in edit mode.
  • Users can upload an existing .html file from the HTML page creation screen.
  • Users can upload HTML pages or folders from the Site Pages library.
  • Users can edit text directly on the page or use the Copilot chat pane for broader content and design changes.
  • Published pages are visible to users who already have permission to view the page; publishing does not grant new permissions.
  • The site-scoped Agent creation entry point will be removed from the + New menu on site pages. New agent creation remains available from the command bar of a document library or list and from the context menu of selected files in a document library.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required before rollout.

Before rollout, you may want to:

  • Inform SharePoint authors about the new HTML page creation, upload, edit, publish, and sharing capabilities.
  • Update internal SharePoint or Copilot guidance if your organization documents page authoring workflows.
  • Review Copilot licensing assignments to confirm which users will have access to Copilot-assisted HTML page creation.
  • Remind users that publishing an HTML page does not grant new permissions.
  • Review: Create, upload, edit, and publish HTML pages in SharePoint.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change store new customer data, if so, where, and is the data cached or permanently stored?Yes. HTML pages created or uploaded by users are stored in the SharePoint Site Pages library according to existing SharePoint storage and retention behavior.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Users can create, upload, edit, publish, and share HTML content as SharePoint pages. Existing SharePoint permissions determine who can access published pages.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Copilot in SharePoint can generate or edit HTML page content based on user prompts and attached files that the user provides or is authorized to access.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can use Copilot in SharePoint to create and edit HTML pages through prompts.
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Access to Copilot-assisted HTML page creation depends on existing Copilot licensing, SharePoint permissions, and organizational controls for Copilot experiences.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: File sharing enabled by default in external (federated) chats
item.description:
[What and why]

We are updating Microsoft Teams file sharing in external (federated) chats by changing the default setting from Disabled to Enabled. Today, admins must explicitly enable file sharing in external chats before users can attach files when collaborating with people outside their organization.

This update simplifies cross-organization collaboration by allowing users to attach files directly in external (federated) chats and automatically applying the required permissions to shared files. Together, these changes remove both the tenant configuration step and the manual permission assignment step that can slow cross-organization collaboration. Existing OneDrive, SharePoint, and security controls continue to govern access. 

Admins retain full control and can disable file sharing or automatic permission assignment at any time using PowerShell.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams external access (federation)
  • Organizations that previously disabled file sharing in external chats
  • Users participating in external 1:1 chats, external group chats, and meeting chats

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • External (federated) 1:1 chats
  • External (federated) group chats
  • Meeting chats
  • Teams desktop app
  • Teams web app

What will happen

  • File sharing in external chats will be enabled by default for all Microsoft 365 tenants.
  • This change applies even if your organization previously configured the setting as Disabled.
  • Organizations that want file sharing in external chats to remain disabled must reapply the disabled setting after rollout.
  • Users will see the Attach file (paperclip) option in external (federated) chats. Previously, users could only paste existing links in external chats.
  • Users can share files by attaching a file or dragging and dropping a file into the compose box.
  • Teams will automatically grant the required permissions to participants in the external chat when a file is uploaded, so users do not need to manually update sharing permissions.
  • Senders can review, modify, or remove sharing permissions before sending a file.
  • Senders can continue to modify or revoke access after a file has been shared.
  • Automatic permission assignment applies only to files uploaded through the attach or drag-and-drop experience.
  • Pasted file links retain their existing permissions and are not automatically shared.
  • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display an External label.
  • Existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing controls continue to govern access.
  • Existing sensitivity labels, domain restrictions, and security protections continue to apply.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action is required only if your organization wants file sharing in external chats to remain disabled.

After rollout reaches your tenant, reapply the following Teams PowerShell setting:

Set-CsTeamsFilesPolicy -Identity Global -FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers Disabled

Verify the setting:

Get-CsTeamsFilesPolicy | Select Identity, FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers

Recommended actions:

  • Review your SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Entra external sharing configuration because these settings continue to govern what external recipients can access.
  • Consider enabling Microsoft Entra B2B for SharePoint and OneDrive external sharing to help external recipients authenticate and access shared files.
  • Inform helpdesk and support teams about this change.
  • Update user training and internal documentation as needed.
  • Communicate to users that:
    • They can attach files directly in chats with people outside the organization.
    • Files attached through the file upload experience are automatically shared with participants in the chat unless permissions are modified.
    • Pasted file links retain their existing permissions.
    • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display an External label.

Optional configuration:

To disable automatic permission assignment while continuing to allow file attachments in external chats:

Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity Global -AutoShareFilesInExternalChats Disabled

If automatic permission assignment is disabled, users may need to manually grant access to shared files before external recipients can open them.

Allow several hours for policy changes to propagate before users see the updated experience.

Learn more:

  • Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Uploaded files can automatically receive permissions for participants in external chats. Existing OneDrive and SharePoint controls continue to govern access.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?Yes. Users can attach and share files directly in external (federated) chats by default.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can enable or disable file sharing in external chats and automatic permission assignment through Teams PowerShell policies.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: Updates to Teams Events licensing for business, frontline, and education customers
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We are updating how Microsoft Teams Events capabilities are organized by license type. Teams Events capabilities will be grouped into foundational event features and advanced event features. This update clarifies which licenses map to each category, attendee limits, and the relationship between Teams Enterprise and Teams Premium licensing.

Foundational event features are available with eligible Teams licenses and support creating and running Teams events.

Advanced event features are included with Teams Enterprise licenses and provide additional controls for event production, management, engagement, customization, and analytics.

License categories:

FrontlineMicrosoft 365 F1, Microsoft 365 F3, Office 365 F3Not included
EnterpriseNot includedOffice 365 E1, E3, E5; Microsoft 365 E3, E5, E7
EducationOffice 365 A1, Microsoft 365 A1, Office 365 A3/A5 for Students, Microsoft 365 A3/A5 for StudentsOffice 365 A3/A5 for Faculty, Microsoft 365 A3/A5 for Faculty

Event capacity:

Maximum attendees with registration1,0003,000
Maximum attendees without registration10,00010,000

Many Teams Events capabilities moved from Teams Premium to Teams Enterprise in April 2026. The new Teams Premium license does not provide Teams Events capabilities. Customers who need all Teams Events features must assign organizers an eligible Teams Enterprise license.

For Teams Events larger than 3,000 attendees, organizations need to purchase attendee capacity packs and assign the licenses to the event organizer. Attendee capacity packs enable events with up to 100,000 attendees.

Microsoft reserves the right to enforce email one-time passcode verification for external event participants to protect service health and guard against fraud or abuse. This enforcement is not tied to a specific SKU tier.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late September 2026 and expect to complete by late September 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Teams admins and licensing admins who manage Teams Events organizer licensing.
  • Teams Events organizers and producers.
  • Organizations using Teams Events across business, frontline, enterprise, education, trial, or legacy Teams Premium licensing.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Teams.
  • Teams Events.
  • Teams licensing.

What will happen:

  • Teams Events capabilities will be organized into foundational and advanced event feature categories.
  • Some features, such as Hide attendee names, will be available for all Teams events customers.
  • Advanced Teams Events capabilities require eligible Teams Enterprise licensing.
  • Teams Premium no longer provides Teams Events capabilities for the new Teams Premium license.
  • Organizations planning events over 3,000 attendees must evaluate attendee capacity pack requirements.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Review licenses assigned to Teams Events organizers.
  • Assign an eligible Teams Enterprise license to organizers who require the full suite of enterprise event capabilities.
  • Evaluate attendee capacity pack requirements for events expected to exceed 3,000 attendees.
  • Update internal support and deployment guidance to reflect the license categories and event limits described in this message.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins manage access to Teams Events capabilities through licensing assignments and related Teams admin controls.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Organizations may need to review organizer licensing and event capacity requirements to ensure Teams Events are configured appropriately.

For more information, see Teams events licensing overview.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Planner: Meeting-created plans will expire after 180 days of inactivity
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Planner plans created from Teams meetings can remain unused long after the meeting ends. To reduce clutter and improve lifecycle management, meeting-created Planner plans with no task activity for 180 consecutive days will automatically expire and be deleted. Only the Planner plan and Planner-specific data are removed. Tasks in Loop and meeting notes remain intact and accessible.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who create or organize Teams meetings that generate Planner plans.
  • Admins and support teams who help users manage or recover Planner plans.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Planner.
  • Microsoft Teams meetings.
  • Loop and meeting notes.

What will happen:

  • Planner plans created from Teams meetings will automatically expire and be deleted after 180 consecutive days with no task activity.
  • Tracking starts at rollout and applies only to new meeting-created plans. Existing plans are out of scope.
  • No plan can be deleted earlier than 180 days after rollout.
  • Activity includes creating, editing, or deleting a task. Viewing or opening a plan does not count as activity.
  • Meeting organizers will receive email notifications 30 days and 7 days before deletion. The email will list affected plans, the last-activity date, and a link to view tasks in Planner.
  • Users can select Keep plan to retain a plan for another 180 days without editing tasks. A plan can be kept as many times as needed.
  • If no action is taken, the plan is deleted on the scheduled date. Deleted plans can be recovered within 30 days through an IT admin request to Microsoft support. After 30 days, deletion is permanent.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required to enable this feature.

To prepare, admins should:

  • Inform users that meeting-created Planner plans inactive for 180 days will automatically expire and be deleted.
  • Explain that advance email notifications will be sent to meeting organizers before deletion.
  • Remind users they can select Keep plan in Planner to retain a plan they still need.
  • Prepare support teams to assist with recovery requests during the 30-day recovery window.
  • Reassure users that tasks stored in Loop and meeting notes are not affected by plan expiration.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Meeting-created Planner plans with no task activity for 180 consecutive days will automatically expire and be deleted. Tasks in Loop and meeting notes remain intact.
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows?Yes. This change introduces automatic expiration and deletion behavior for inactive meeting-created Planner plans, with advance user notification and a 30-day recovery window.

item.title: [planForChange] Video recap in Microsoft Teams supports more languages
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Video recap in Microsoft Teams uses AI to create a narrated highlight video from a recorded and transcribed meeting. It combines key meeting content with short video clips, helping users catch up without watching the full recording. With this update, Video recap is expanding support to 23 languages across 31 locale variants

The first set of supported languages includes: English, Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese,Spanish. Arabic, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Hebrew, Hungarian, Korean, Norwegian, Polish, Russian, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, and Ukrainian. Regional variants are supported for English, Chinese, French, Portuguese, and Spanish. 

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (WW): We will begin rolling out on late September 2026 and expect to complete by late September 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license will be able to access Video recap for eligible meetings in the supported languages.

For a Video recap to be available, the meeting must:

  • Be between 10 and 90 minutes long.
  • Be recorded and transcribed with cloud recording enabled.
  • Meet the existing Microsoft 365 Copilot eligibility requirements.

After a meeting, users can open the meeting chat, select **Recap**, and then select **Video recap**. They can also open a past meeting from the Teams calendar and select **View recap**.

No separate Video recap file is created. Video recap data is stored with the original Teams recording in SharePoint or OneDrive.

Video recaps are AI-generated. Users should review the content for accuracy.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No user action is required before this rollout.

You may want to:

  • Inform your help desk about the expanded language support.
  • Update internal training and documentation for Video recap.
  • Confirm that eligible users have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and that your existing meeting recording and transcription policies meet the Video recap requirements.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?The feature introduces or updates a user-facing AI or Copilot experience as described in this message.

item.title: [planForChange] ADO MCP in Copilot
item.description:
[What and Why:]

The Azure DevOps (ADO) MCP Connector introduces a protocol-based integration between Azure DevOps and Microsoft 365 Copilot Deep Work. This enables agents to access and analyze work items, bugs, and project data through natural language, reducing the need for manual navigation and query writing when analyzing development work.

Built on Model Context Protocol (MCP), this connector supports multi-step, agent-driven workflows and lays the foundation for write actions. Write actions are gated by user confirmation and configuration support. This supports business process automation by helping organizations bring project context into Copilot experiences while preserving admin controls.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who use Microsoft 365 Copilot Deep Work to analyze Azure DevOps work items, bugs, and project data.
  • Admins who manage Microsoft 365 Copilot data access and Azure DevOps integration settings.
  • Organizations that use Azure DevOps for project planning, engineering workflows, or issue tracking.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot Deep Work
  • Azure DevOps
  • Azure DevOps MCP Connector
  • Microsoft 365 admin center

What will happen:

  • Users will be able to ask Microsoft 365 Copilot natural-language questions about Azure DevOps work items, bugs, and project data.
  • Copilot agents will be able to access and analyze Azure DevOps data through the ADO MCP Connector when allowed by admin configuration.
  • User queries and relevant Copilot context may be shared with Azure DevOps to complete requests.
  • Azure DevOps data may be returned to Copilot for responses and supported actions.
  • The connector supports multi-step, agent-driven workflows.
  • Write actions are supported as a foundation capability and are gated by user confirmation and configuration support.
  • Admins can configure the Azure DevOps data in Microsoft 365 Copilot setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Before rollout, admins should:

  • Review the Azure DevOps data in Microsoft 365 Copilot setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Choose the appropriate access scope: All users, Specific users and groups, or No user.
  • Review the data-sharing notice and applicable Azure DevOps and Microsoft product terms before allowing access.
  • Notify affected users and support teams before rollout.
  • Update internal guidance for using Azure DevOps data with Microsoft 365 Copilot Deep Work.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?User queries and relevant Copilot context may be shared with Azure DevOps to complete requests, and Azure DevOps work items, bugs, and project data may be returned to Copilot for responses and supported actions.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?The ADO MCP Connector enables Copilot agents to access and analyze Azure DevOps work items, bugs, and project data through natural language and multi-step agent workflows.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Users can ask Microsoft 365 Copilot natural-language questions about Azure DevOps project data and receive responses grounded in Azure DevOps content.
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Admins can configure the Azure DevOps data in Microsoft 365 Copilot setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center and choose All users, Specific users and groups, or No user.
Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves?Write actions are gated by user confirmation, and user access depends on admin configuration. The user can choose whether to initiate Copilot interactions with Azure DevOps data.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Unified management of app and agent availability and installation in Teams, Outlook, and the Microsoft 365 app
item.description:
Updated September 25, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience.

What it is

Microsoft is rolling out a new feature to streamline how app and agent availability and installation is managed across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Until now, IT admins configured availability and installation settings separately in both the Microsoft 365 Admin Center (MAC) and the Teams Admin Center (TAC), which led to mismatches. With this update, you’ll be able to unify availability and installation policies for apps and agents across both portals, making app management more consistent and efficient.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931, 485712 and 503105.

When this will happen: 

We will begin rolling out this feature late September 2025. Rollout timeline for phase 3 will be announced later.

A: Unify app availability across admin centers

1. Phase 1 – Default Tenant Unification of App/Agent Availability

We will begin rolling out this feature at the end of September 2025. This initial phase targets tenants that have never modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock in either the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Teams admin center. At the end of this phase, agent and app manageability will be unified across both Microsoft 365 admin center and Teams admin center ensuring agent and Microsoft 365 apps availability policies are in alignment for all future administrative changes. This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931.

2.Phase 2 – Modified Tenants Unification of App/Agent Availability

This phase targets tenants that have previously modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock settings in either admin center. These tenants will be transitioned to a unified management experience across both Microsoft 365 and Teams admin centers.

  • For tenants with no agent or app availability differences across both admin centers, guidance will be provided to help maintain unified availability policy for all future changes.

For tenants with agent or app availability differences across both admin centers, a wizard in the Teams admin center will help identify affected agents and apps and guide through resolving discrepancies.

  • As part of this phase we will also enable administrators to manage Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications within their tenant through org-wide settings for third-party apps. This has been rolled out completely for all tenants.
  • This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 485712 & 503105.

This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants. Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

Note: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

3. Phase 3 – Automatic Unification (Future)

Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase. We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

B: Unify app installation across admin centers

In this phase, app and agent installation management is unified across the Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center. Admins can manage supported app and agent installations from either portal, and changes remain synchronized across both admin centers.

No additional action is required by admins. Existing installation assignments will be synchronized across both admin centers for eligible tenants.

Eligible tenants: Any tenant that moved to the unified availability state as part of Phase 1 or Phase 2, or moves as part of Phase 3 in the future, will automatically receive this feature once unified.

Timeline: We will release this feature end of September 2026 for eligible tenants.

Important: App installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies. App installations previously made through app setup policies are not unified as part of this change.

  • This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 567883

How this will affect your organization

Before this rollout, managing Teams apps that also work in Outlook and the Microsoft 365 app was fragmented across two admin centers:

  • the Integrated apps and Agent apps pages in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and
  • the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

This sometimes resulted in inconsistent availability settings for the same app.

With Unified agent app management, admins can manage apps and agents from either the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Teams admin center. Availability settings will remain synchronized across both, ensuring a consistent management experience.

What you can expect:

  • You’ll gain a consolidated view of agent and Microsoft 365 app availability across both Microsoft 365 and Teams admin centers.
  • Changes made in either admin center to the agent and app availability will automatically apply across all supported hosts.
  • Organization-wide defaults for both admin centers will be in sync and govern app availability across Teams, Outlook, and the Microsoft 365 copilot app.

What you need to do to prepare

To ensure a smooth transition, review your tenant-level and individual agent/app settings (app allow/block & user availability) in both the Microsoft 365 Admin Center and the Teams Admin Center. If different departments within your organization manage these settings, we suggest coordinating efforts to complete the review collaboratively.

This update will be rolled out automatically by the stated date, and no immediate action is required. However, it's a good time to update any internal documentation related to agent and app management policies.

Learn more: Unified agent and app availability management across Microsoft 365 and Teams Admin Centers - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Copilot: New ways to work across Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft 365

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Copilot: Evolving the Copilot pricing model and new FinOps capabilities for AI
item.description:
[What and why:]

We are evolving Copilot pricing model as AI gets more capable with longer and more complex work. Everyday AI remains covered by the Copilot user subscription license (USL), priced per user per month, including model selection and Auto, which weighs accuracy, speed, and cost on each request to route to the model and level of reasoning effort best suited to the job. Advanced AI, including new advanced frontier models, may now be available through usage-based billing (UBB) with Copilot Credits. For more information, read Evolution of the Copilot pricing model.

Users may encounter UBB:

  • When using a frontier model or advanced AI or
  • When they hit a limit, with an option to extend their use through Copilot Credits

UBB capabilities will be visible to all end users, however these capabilities are not enabled or functional within Enterprise tenants until an admin creates a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Only then will credits to use UBB features by consumed.

You can control and manage consumption billing across your organization through the admin policies, spending limits, and monitoring tools you configure.

We are also releasing new FinOps for AI capabilities to help you understand and manage usage, connect cost to value, and make informed decisions: 

  • Cost management in Microsoft 365 admin center is expanding beyond Copilot Cowork and Work IQ APIs to support Copilot Code, Copilot Managed Runtime, and advanced work for SharePoint and OneDrive in Copilot. In October, support will also extend to agents built through Microsoft Copilot Studio.
  • When configuring a spending policy in Microsoft 365 admin center, admins can assign models and effort levels by group to balance cost and business impact, including which models Auto can select in Cowork. This capability is rolling out for Cowork, with more workloads planned.
  • The consumption dashboard in Insights is designed to help leaders get a clearer view of how Cowork helps their teams complete meaningful work—not just how often they use it. By connecting credit consumption with outcomes, organizations can identify high-value scenarios and compare results with the resources invested.
  • End users can view their UBB spend within the Cowork experience with the ability to see credit usage, remaining credits, and credit history, with banners alerting them as they approach their limits.
  • Administrators can now edit billing methods for existing spend policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

For more additional information, read New FinOps for AI capabilities: Control spend, measure value, and optimize for impact.

Learn more about new features coming to Copilot, including advanced capabilities in SharePoint which will roll out with UBB, in the Microsoft Copilot: New ways to work across Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft 365 message center post.

[Rollout schedule:]

UBB will begin to roll out in Copilot in Q4 CY2026. UBB will also be enabled as part of the Frontier public preview experience.

All FinOps capabilities listed above are available in preview in September 2026. End-user visibility into Copilot Credit usage, remaining credits, and credit history is generally available in September 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Administrators can use cost management in the Microsoft 365 admin center to manage usage-based billing, assign access and spending policies, monitor Copilot Credit usage and spend, view remaining credit capacity, and set limits and alerts. Controls may vary by service.

Users will see frontier models and advanced AI with UBB in Copilot as those features become available. UBB capabilities are visible in product by default. If a user has a spending policy assigned to them, they will be able to consume Copilot Credits as part of UBB.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  • No action is required to continue using capabilities included as part of the USL
  • Manage usage-based billing and Copilot Credit consumption by configuring spending policies.

Additional Information

  • Understanding the user subscription license (USL) and usage-based billing (UBB)
  • Usage-Based Billing and Cost Management for Copilot Credits
  • Managing AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing
  • Discovery setting for AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing
  • Copilot Credits Licensing Guide

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change store new customer data? These changes introduce consumption tracking, credit usage monitoring, spend history, and cost management capabilities. Usage and billing-related data will be collected and surfaced through consumption dashboards and spend management views. 
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed? New frontier models and advanced AI capabilities may process existing Microsoft 365 content when used through Copilot experiences. 
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with customer data? These changes include new frontier models and advanced AI capabilities through usage-based billing and introduce model selection controls, Auto model selection governance, and expanded AI workload support. 
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI? Users can access frontier models, advanced AI experiences, and usage-based extensions when limits are reached. The embedded spend management experience also exposes consumption information directly within the Copilot experience. 
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities? New FinOps capabilities expand cost management, consumption monitoring, spending policies, model assignment by group, outcome measurement, and credit consumption reporting. Administrators gain additional oversight and governance controls. 
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership? Administrators must create spending policies before Copilot Credits can be consumed, with group-based governance controls.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Use Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents in declarative agents

Microsoft is introducing support for Microsoft Agent 365 agents that implement the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, allowing them to be used as connected agents in declarative agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

This enhancement expands the types of external agent services that declarative agents can connect to. In addition to existing support for OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, declarative agents can now connect to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling natural language interactions and support for more complex workflows.

This feature gives developers greater flexibility when building declarative agents while providing administrators centralized management and governance through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late August 2026 and expected to complete by late September 2026
  • Microsoft internal deployment (MSIT): Available now

  • Microsoft 365 administrators who manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Developers building declarative agents with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Users who are assigned access to approved Microsoft Agent 365 agents

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Declarative agents

What will happen

  • Administrators can install Microsoft Agent 365 agents that support the Agent2Agent protocol from the All agents page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Declarative agents can use approved Agent2Agent-enabled agents as connected agents.
  • Agent2Agent support is added alongside existing support for OpenAPI and MCP server connections.
  • Users cannot install Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents themselves.
  • Administrators can review Agent2Agent-connected agents from the Connected agents tab in the declarative agent details page before approving their use.

Before rollout:

  • Determine which Agent2Agent-enabled agents should be made available to users in your organization.

Consider notifying administrators and developers in your organization about the availability of Agent2Agent-connected agents and the associated review and approval process.

Organizations should review how these connected agents interact with customer data before approving them for use.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] SharePoint: Improved site metadata size reporting
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is improving how site metadata size is reported in SharePoint. The calculation will include document library field data, giving admins a more complete view of a site’s metadata usage.

Nothing about your content changes. No content is added, moved, or removed, and the site metadata size limit remains 1 TB per site.

Because the calculation is more complete, reported metadata size may be higher for some sites. For most sites, the difference will be small and nothing else will change. Some sites may show a size at or above the 1 TB limit once the updated calculation is applied.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability, Worldwide: We will begin rolling out on October 20, 2026.
  • Sites already identified as expected to reach or exceed the 1 TB metadata limit will be excluded from the initial rollout to provide additional time to reduce their metadata usage before the correction is applied.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • SharePoint admins who monitor site storage and metadata usage.
  • Organizations with SharePoint sites that are close to or above the 1 TB site metadata limit.
  • Site owners and users of sites that receive metadata warnings or enforcement messages.

Platforms/Services:

  • SharePoint Online.
  • SharePoint Storage Metrics.
  • SharePoint document libraries and lists.

What will happen:

  • Most organizations will see no change in behavior.
  • The visible difference is that reported site metadata size may be higher than before because document library field data is included in the calculation.
  • For sites that cross the 1 TB metadata limit after the correction, the site is blocked from adding new metadata until usage is brought back under the limit.
  • Existing content stays in place and remains accessible.
  • SharePoint shows a warning or error message when the site is close to, or has reached, the metadata limit.
  • For sites that reach 80% of the metadata limit, admins can review the metadata size breakdown on the Storage Metrics page.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is needed for most organizations.

If you see a metadata warning for a site, review its metadata usage and take steps to reduce it:

  • Check the Storage Metrics page for the site. For sites at or above 80% of the metadata limit, the metadata size breakdown is available on this page.
  • Delete unneeded items from your lists and document libraries.
  • Delete older file versions in your document libraries.
  • Remove duplicate files across lists and libraries.
  • Follow the steps provided in the in-product warning message.
  • Re-check the Storage Metrics page after making changes.

item.title: [planForChange] Final reminder: Microsoft Project Online retires on September 30, 2026
item.description:
[What and why:]

Microsoft Project Online will retire on September 30, 2026.  

If users are still using Project Online, they will see an in-app banner announcing the retirement. 

If your organization will not be fully migrated by September 30, 2026, we highly recommend you contact a Microsoft partner immediately to make a migration plan and let your Microsoft account team know your plans.  

At Microsoft, we are committed to empowering every organization with a unified, AI-powered and collaborative work management experience that brings together tasks, plans, and projects in one seamless platform. As part of this commitment, we announced the retirement of Project Online last September. The decision reflects our focus on delivering solutions that are modern, scalable, and future-ready—enabling organizations to benefit from the latest innovations in AI, automation, and collaboration.  Moving to our next-generation platforms brings enhanced productivity, deeper integration with Microsoft 365, and new capabilities designed for the way people work today and tomorrow. 

This update is exclusive to Project Online and does not affect Project desktop/Project Online desktop, Project Server, or Planner.  

We recognize that every organization is unique, with different project management needs and technical requirements. To ensure a smooth transition and continued success, Microsoft is providing three clear paths forward. 

  1. Microsoft Planner: For organizations seeking a modern, cloud-first, and AI-powered project management experience, Planner is designed for flexibility, collaboration, and scalability—empowering teams to manage everything from simple tasks to complex projects in one unified platform. The premium features of Planner included in our Planner and Project Plan 3 license, offer advanced features such as portfolios, baselines, dependencies, and Gantt charts. 
  2. Project Server Subscription Edition: For organizations with advanced project and portfolio management (PPM) requirements, or those needing a short-term solution before moving to the cloud, Project Server Subscription Edition offers comprehensive tools for planning, scheduling, and resource management—built on the latest SharePoint Server technology. 
  3. Project Operations: For Dynamics ERP customers, especially those focused on timesheets and resource scheduling. 

[Rollout schedule:]

Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD:  September 30, 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

  • After Project Online is retired, you will no longer be able to access your projects or any associated data within the service.  
  • To avoid disruption and potential data loss, it's essential that you complete your transition to any of the alternatives before the retirement date.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  • Identify a Microsoft Partner immediately to help you move off Project Online by month end. To find a partner, contact your Microsoft Sales Representative for a list of recommended partners in your region.

item.title: [stayInformed] Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID
item.description:

Beginning on September 2026, automatic migrations of agents without Entra Agent ID to Microsoft Entra Agent ID were also initiated. How does this affect me?
Migrating your agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID helps your organization build, discover, govern, and protect agent identities across services by using a unified platform.

Key benefits include:
  • Audit logging in Microsoft Entra ID.
  • Agent lifecycle management.
  • Integration with Entra ID Governance.
  • Visibility of connector permissions as API permissions on the agent identity, so Entra and Microsoft 365 admins can see what an agent can do without opening Power Platform admin center.
  • Ability to target those connector permissions with Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies (for example, network location, device compliance, or risk conditions).
To find out if your agent has been migrated already been migrated or if there are any agents that remain to be migrated in your tenant, you can use the Advisor recommendation.

What action do I need to take?
We recommend identifying and migrating your eligible agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID. To perform this mitigation, please follow the steps listed below:
  1. Confirm that Power Platform inventory is enabled for your tenant.
  2. In the Power Platform admin center, go to Actions > Recommendations > Active, and open Migrate Copilot Studio agents to Microsoft Entra Agent ID for enhanced agent governance.
  3. In the recommendation pane, expand Why is this important?, and review the migration guidance.
  4. Review the eligible agents. Use Suggested migration order and Migration notes to choose an initial pilot or the next migration batch. The table also provides information such as environment, environment type, owner, recent activity, and authentication method.
  5. Select the checkbox next to each agent you want to migrate. You can select one agent or multiple eligible agents. The Migrate button becomes available and the action bar shows the number of agents selected.
  6. Select Migrate, review the confirmation, and confirm the migration. Start with a small batch of noncritical agents.
  7. Review the Action, Action state, and Action date columns for each selected agent. To review actions across recommendations, select the Action history tab.
  8. Coordinate a validation window with the makers who own the agents.
  9. After migration, validate each agent's channels, authentication, actions, connectors, flows, and integrations before migrating another batch.
  10. Review Microsoft Entra sign-in logs and applicable Conditional Access results. If an agent does not pass validation, revert it before continuing.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Enhanced security and access controls for Outlook attachments
item.description:
Updated September 23, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

As part of our overall security initiatives, we’ve created a separate internal application configuration for Outlook attachments, therefore, all standard security and authentication flows will be handled separately. Moreover, Conditional Access policies are now enforced for Outlook attachment operations. Users who don’t meet company policies won’t be able to download, preview, or upload classic attachments (this includes inline images). Policies assigned to Exchange and Office cloud applications will be inherited by the attachment application by default. Continuous Access Evaluation is not included in the initial rollout but will follow up soon.

[Rollout schedule:]

Available now.

[Impact on your organization:]

  • Your existing policies now cover attachments. Conditional Access policies you have already scoped to Exchange and Office cloud applications will be enforced for attachment scenarios as well. No new policies need to be created.
  • Users out of compliance will be blocked from attachments. If a user's session no longer satisfies a Conditional Access policy — for example, a non-compliant device, a blocked location, or a network change that triggers CAE re-evaluation — attachment operations will be blocked.
  • These are separate follow-up changes we expect to land in the upcoming weeks. We’ll keep you updated on the readiness and rollout of these enhancements:
    • User sign in prompt for remediation. We're currently working on a solution to prompt the user for sign in to recover functionalities when possible. This will depend on the policy configuration; if the user is not compliant, they won’t be able to use attachment-related tasks. We’ll provide an update to customers once we start rolling out this enhancement.
    • Enable Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE). CAE isn’t supported for this new application configuration yet. We’ll update this message with additional content when it becomes available.  

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  1. Review how your Office and Exchange policies apply to attachments.
    1. Attachment operations are now handled by their own application, which by default inherits the Conditional Access policies you've assigned to Office and Exchange. Confirm those conditions are what you intend to enforce for attachments.
    2. If you’ve intentionally excluded Exchange online from a policy, that exclusion doesn't carry over to attachments, so users in scope can reach their mail but will be blocked from downloading, previewing, or uploading attachments.
    3. To manage attachment policies separate from mail, you can either exclude the attachment application from a policy or target it in a policy of its own. Both require a one-time setup step in your tenant — see Appendix: Excluding attachments from a policy.
  2. Update your help desk documentation. Support staff should know that attachment access failures may now result from a Conditional Access policy, and that the remediation is the same as for Outlook — return to a compliant device or network and re-authenticate.
  3. Notify users if you enforce strict Conditional Access policies, so they understand attachment actions may now be blocked under the same conditions that already block access to their mailbox.

[Appendix:]

Excluding attachments from a policy

Attachment operations are handled by an application named OwaDownloadAttachments (application Id: e4f2bb2d-a4d0-4eab-aac6-a8b83471cf64 ). Before you can exclude it from a Conditional Access policy, a service principal for it must exist in your tenant. This is a one-time step you'll need to complete first.

Step 1: Create the service principal

You'll need the Cloud Application Administrator or Global Administrator role.

  1. Open Graph Explorer and sign in as an administrator of your tenant.
  2. Run:

POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals

Request body: { "appId": "e4f2bb2d-a4d0-4eab-aac6-a8b83471cf64" }

Consent to Application.ReadWrite.All scope is required.

A successful request returns 201 Created with a display name of OwaDownloadAttachments. If the request reports that the service principal already exists, continue to Step 2.

Step 2: Exclude it from the policy

  1. Click on View or Edit on the Conditional Access Policy you want to update.
  2. Under Target resources, select the Exclude tab.
  3. Choose Select resources, search for OwaDownloadAttachments, and select it.
  4. Save the policy.

Repeat Step 2 for each policy you want attachment operations exempted from.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Enhanced delegated calling with delegate call access restrictions and join notifications
item.description:
Updated September 22, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and Why:]

Microsoft is enhancing Microsoft Teams call delegation with new controls that provide greater privacy, transparency, and control during active calls. Delegators will be able to lock active calls to prevent delegate participation and optionally enable warning tones that notify participants whenever a delegate joins or resumes a call. These enhancements help users manage sensitive conversations more effectively while improving awareness during delegated call handling.

This message is associated with Roadmap ID 567306.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early August 2026 and expect to complete by mid-August 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-August 2026 and expect to complete by mid-August 2026.
  • General Availability (GCC, GCC High): We will begin rolling out in mid-August 2026 and expect to complete by late August 2026.
  • General Availability (DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-August 2026 and expect to complete by end of October 2026 (previously mid-September).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users with Microsoft Teams call delegation configured.
  • Executives, administrative assistants, managers, and support personnel who use delegated calling.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Teams Calling
  • Teams desktop
  • Teams web

What will happen:

  • A new Lock an Ongoing Call capability will be available to delegators.

    • Screenshot 1: During an active call, delegators can use the new Lock call control from the meeting toolbar to restrict delegate participation in sensitive conversations:

    Screenshot 2: Delegators can lock an active Teams call directly from the Calls experience, preventing delegates from joining or resuming the call until it is unlocked:

  • Delegators can lock an active call to prevent delegates from:
    • Resuming a call that has been placed on hold.
    • Joining an ongoing active call.
  • Delegates will continue to see locked calls in their call history.
  • Delegates will be unable to participate in locked calls until the delegator unlocks the call.
  • A new optional Warning Tone for Delegate Participation setting will be available.

    • Screenshot 3: New call delegation settings allow users to enable an audible notification that alerts participants whenever a delegate joins or resumes a delegated call:

  • When enabled, all call participants will hear an audible notification when a delegate:
    • Joins an active call.
    • Resumes a held call.
  • The feature increases transparency regarding delegate participation in live calls.
  • This change will be available by default to users with call delegation configured.
  • No existing call delegation workflows are removed.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No immediate administrative action is required.

Recommended actions:

  • Review how call delegation is used within your organization.
  • Inform users who utilize delegated calling about the new lock and notification capabilities.
  • Update internal Teams calling documentation and training materials.
  • Notify help desk and support teams of the new user experience to prepare for potential questions.
  • Evaluate whether the delegate participation warning tone should be recommended for users handling confidential or sensitive conversations.
  • Monitor Microsoft's official documentation for feature configuration details as rollout approaches.

Learn more: Share a phone line with a delegate in Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Support (will be updated for GA rollout)

[Compliance Considerations:]

Compliance Question Explanation
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions? The feature introduces new delegated calling controls that affect how delegates can participate in ongoing calls. It also adds an optional audible notification that informs all call participants when a delegate joins or resumes a delegated call, increasing transparency during communications.
Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves? Delegators can lock and unlock ongoing calls and can enable or disable the warning tone notification setting for delegate participation.
